bios.meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct: Marie Curie was born Maria Skłodowska on November 7, 1867, in Warsaw, Poland. She studied physics and mathematics at the Flying University, a secret institution for women, and later moved to Paris to pursue further education at the Sorbonne, where she earned her degree in physics in 1893. Curie went on to earn her doctorate in physics from the Sorbonne in 1903 and became a professor of general physics at the University of Paris in 1906. She was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903, along with her husband Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, for their pioneering work on radioactivity, and again in 1911, this time alone, for her work on the isolation of pure radium.
bios.qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct: Marie Curie was born in 1867 in Warsaw, Poland. She is renowned for her pioneering work in the field of radioactivity and was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, which she received twice, in Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911.
bios.mistralai/ministral-8b-2512: Marie Curie (born **Maria Skłodowska**) was born on **November 7, 1867**, in **Warsaw, Poland** (then part of the Russian Empire). A pioneering physicist and chemist, she conducted groundbreaking research on **radioactivity**, coining the term and isolating **polonium** (named after her homeland) and **radium**. In **1903**, she shared the **Nobel Prize in Physics** with her husband, Pierre Curie, and Henri Becquerel for their work on radioactivity, and in **1911**, she became the first person (and only woman at the time) to win a **Nobel Prize in two different fields** (Chemistry for radium isolation). Curie died on **July 4, 1934**, in **Sallanches, France**, from **aplastic anemia**, likely caused by prolonged exposure to radioactive materials.

bios.meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct: Charles Robert Darwin was born on February 12, 1809, in Shrewsbury, Shropshire, England.
